Definition: apparently from G2046 (compare G2045); to interrogate; by implication, to request:--ask, beseech, desire, intreat, pray. Compare G4441.
BiblicalUsage: Erōtáō means to ask — to interrogate, to request, to beseech. The disciples ask Jesus when He will restore the kingdom; Jesus asks the Father for His own; and He tells His disciples to ask the Father in His name. It is the word for asking that expects an answer.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe erōtáō is the word for prayer as asking: Jesus asks the Father, and He tells us to ask too. I hold that asking is not begging — it is the way children speak to a Father who hears.
